headline: INTERTANKO weekly Hormuz southern-route transits averaging >30/day despite continued Gulf ship attacks
dek: Vessels continue to use the southern US-facilitated route through the Strait of Hormuz, averaging >30 transits/day, ~90% tankers. Attacks on commercial vessels continue across the Gulf; two vessels sank after earlier Gulf of Oman attacks (a containership in Hormuz and bulk carrier Cape Dao);…
sources: INTERTANKO weekly security update, reported by Safety4Sea
fault_line: Is Hormuz actually open (>30 ships a day on the escorted route) or effectively shut (PortWatch counted 4) — whose number do you trust?

sections.what_happened: Vessels continue to use the southern US-facilitated route through the Strait of Hormuz, averaging >30 transits/day, ~90% tankers. Attacks on commercial vessels continue across the Gulf; two vessels sank after earlier Gulf of Oman attacks (a containership in Hormuz and bulk carrier Cape Dao); neither wreck threatens surface navigation. INTERTANKO says no credible evidence supports Iranian claims that vessels struck mines, and Iranian attacked-ship counts exceed credibly evidenced incidents. It expects Gulf shipping attacks to continue, US response unlikely to extend significantly beyond point defence in the Hormuz area. A third US carrier battle group is expected early November; unclear whether routine replacement or capability increase ahead of possible renewed hostilities. Situation broadly unchanged until the Nov 3 US midterm outcome. In the Red Sea, Ansar Allah have conducted no maritime operations for some time, renewed attacks not expected imminently, but capability retained; Ansar Allah effort is focused on fighting Yemen's government and long-range strikes on Saudi infrastructure; UK has deployed fighter aircraft supporting Saudi Arabia, with no expected impact on Red Sea-registered (Red Ensign Group) shipping. Black Sea: two vessels struck in the preceding week, one near Odesa, one near Sochi.
sections.what_verified: Single primary-source family (INTERTANKO's own update) via Safety4Sea; Safety4Sea and INTERTANKO have NO declared tier in the source registry, so the count is reported with attribution and is NOT independently corroborated. The >30/day figure is route-specific (southern US-facilitated route) and is NOT reconcilable with the stale IMF PortWatch all-transit count below without a methodology note.
sections.what_disputed: PORTWATCH BACKBONE (portwatch-2026-10-26.json, STALE, lag 8 days): IMF PortWatch counted 4 total transits through Hormuz on 2026-10-18 (2 tankers), 7-day average 3.71 vs a calendar-2025 baseline of 85.53/day. INTERTANKO's >30/day (southern route only) and PortWatch's 4 (all transits, different methodology/date) cannot both describe the same flow; the gap is UNRESOLVED and must be flagged on screen, never averaged or smoothed. Separately, CENTCOM's 3,000 vessels / 1.5bn barrels / 95% safe claims (recorded 0100-01, repeated today via Anadolu/MENAFN) are claimant figures, not counted transits. UrduPoint/Neptune's ~492 vessels waiting at Gulf anchorages (recorded 1700-03) measures anchorage counts, not transits.
sections.why_matters: Hormuz by the Numbers: the tanker association says 30+ ships a day are moving — but the counted data says 4. One of these numbers is measuring something different, and the gap is the story.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Safety4Sea Oct 26 10:22 UTC = 14:22 , in no prior scan today) -- INTERTANKO weekly update: Hormuz southern-route transits averaging >30/day despite continued Gulf ship attacks; Ansar Allah maritime ops subdued

totw_analysis: Our read: Hormuz by the Numbers: the tanker association says 30+ ships a day are moving — but the counted data says 4. One of these numbers is measuring something different, and the gap is the story. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Hormuz actually open (>30 ships a day on the escorted route) or effectively shut (PortWatch counted 4) — whose number do you trust?
